It forks the WS-C glass-cockpit server\n3\t(`sigil.ui.server`) verbatim in shape (ThreadingHTTPServer + BaseHTTPRequestHandler, the strict\n4\tCSP/nosniff/no-referrer header set, the body cap + 30s timeout, the never-log-auth `log_message`,\n5\tthe SSE structure, the anti-DNS-rebinding Host/Origin/Referer gate) and changes ONLY three things:\n6\t\n7\t  • THE BIND. It binds a `bind_ok` address (loopback or a PRIVATE/WireGuard address) — NEVER\n8\t    0.0.0.0 / a public address. The constructor asserts this; the CLI asserts it too. This is the\n9\t    non-negotiable exposure guard: the tunnel, not the transport, is the network boundary.\n10\t\n11\t  • THE AUTH. There is NO wire bearer secret (the ui's printed token is gone). Authentication IS a\n12\t    per-request Ed25519 signature the phone makes with ITS OWN owner-authorized device key — the\n13\t    Wave-1 device envelope (`bridge.envelope`). The server verifies the signature against the\n14\t    owner-minted authorized-device set (recomputed PER REQUEST so a revocation takes effect at once),\n15\t    binds the authenticated envelope `action` to the endpoint it hit (a `read:pending` envelope can\n16\t    never reach the more-sensitive `read:recall`), applies a wallclock timestamp-freshness window\n17\t    (injectable clock), and for EFFECTFUL actions (panic/relay) additionally runs the envelope's\n18\t    strict monotonic-nonce replay gate (`consume(effectful=True)`). The owner trust-root is NEVER used\n19\t    to sign anything here — the phone signs, the server only verifies.\n20\t\n21\t  • THE ALLOWLIST. The anti-rebind Host/Origin allowlist is derived from the REAL bound address (plus\n22\t    the loopback pair when bound to loopback, for dev), not a hardcoded 127.0.0.1.\n23\t\n24\tEverything sensitive stays off the minimal frames: `/api/pending` and the SSE stream carry only\n25\t`{seq, tier, kind}` — never a subject, never a payload, never a secret. TLS wrapping is a LATER\n26\tslice; this is plain HTTP inside the tunnel. Offense-free.\"\"\"\n27\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n28\t\n29\timport base64\n30\timport ipaddress\n31\timport json\n32\timport time\n33\tfrom http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer\n34\tfrom pathlib import Path\n35\tfrom urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse\n36\t\n37\tfrom ..config import SPINE_PATH\n38\tfrom ..governor.identity import owner_pubkey\n39\tfrom ..mesh import authorized_devices\n40\tfrom ..spine.store import SpineStore\n41\tfrom ..spine.verify import verify_record\n42\tfrom .daemon import BridgeDaemon, bind_ok\n43\tfrom .envelope import consume, verify_envelope\n44\tfrom .notifier import PushNotifier\n45\t\n46\t_WEBAPP = Path(__file__).parent / \"webapp\"       # the PWA is a later slice — served if present, else 404\n47\t_CSP = \"default-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'\"\n48\t_DEFAULT_PORT = 8722\n49\t_TS_WINDOW = 120.0                               # ± seconds a request timestamp may differ from the server clock\n50\t\n51\t# Each network endpoint declares the ONE envelope action that authorizes it. Binding the\n52\t# authenticated action to the endpoint stops a captured lesser-scoped envelope (e.g. `read:pending`,\n53\t# which leaks only {seq,tier,kind}) from being replayed against a more-sensitive endpoint (e.g.\n54\t# `read:recall`, which surfaces the owner's on-screen OCR history). `/api/graph` piggybacks on the\n55\t# `read:snapshot` scope: graph returns only aggregate health, strictly LESS sensitive than the\n56\t# snapshot, so a snapshot-scoped envelope reaching it is not an escalation (and a lesser envelope\n57\t# still cannot reach it).\n58\t_READ_ACTION = {\n59\t    \"/api/pending\": \"read:pending\",\n60\t    \"/api/snapshot\": \"read:snapshot\",\n61\t    \"/api/graph\": \"read:snapshot\",\n62\t    \"/api/stream\": \"read:stream\",\n63\t    \"/api/recall\": \"read:recall\",\n64\t}\n65\t\n66\t\n67\tclass BridgeServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):\n68\t    daemon_threads = True\n69\t\n70\t    def __init__(self, addr, handler, *, spine_path, trusted_pubkey=None, clock=None,\n71\t                 ts_window: float = _TS_WINDOW):\n72\t        host = addr[0]\n73\t        if not bind_ok(host):\n74\t            raise ValueError(\n75\t                f\"refusing to bind {host!r}: the bridge binds loopback or a PRIVATE (WireGuard) \"\n76\t                f\"address only — never 0.0.0.0 / an unspecified / a public address\")\n77\t        super().__init__(addr, handler)\n78\t        self.spine_path = Path(spine_path)\n79\t        # the owner PUBLIC key is the trust anchor (injectable for tests); NO private key ever lives here\n80\t        self.trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n81\t        self.clock = clock or time.time          # injectable wallclock so the freshness gate is deterministic\n82\t        self.ts_window = ts_window\n83\t        port = self.server_address[1]            # the ACTUAL bound port (correct even for port 0)\n84\t        hosts = {f\"{host}:{port}\"}\n85\t        origins = {f\"http://{host}:{port}\"}\n86\t        if ipaddress.ip_address(host).is_loopback:   # dev convenience only — not added for a WG bind\n87\t            hosts |= {f\"127.0.0.1:{port}\", f\"localhost:{port}\"}\n88\t            origins |= {f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\", f\"http://localhost:{port}\"}\n89\t        self.allowed_hosts = frozenset(hosts)\n90\t        self.allowed_origins = frozenset(origins)\n91\t\n92\t    def store(self) -> SpineStore:\n93\t        return SpineStore(self.spine_path)       # fresh read each request (cheap, current)\n94\t\n95\t    def daemon(self) -> BridgeDaemon:\n96\t        return BridgeDaemon(self.store(), trusted_pubkey=self.trusted_pubkey)\n97\t\n98\t\n99\tdef _json_bytes(obj) -> bytes:\n100\t    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode(\"utf-8\")\n101\t\n102\t\n103\tclass Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):\n104\t    server_version = \"sigil-bridge/1.0\"\n105\t    timeout = 30                                  # per-connection socket timeout (no hung reader)\n106\t    _MAX_BODY = 65536                             # bodies are tiny; 0.0.0.0 / :: → refuse\n26\t        return False\n27\t    return ip.is_loopback or ip.is_private\n28\t\n29\t\n30\tclass BridgeDaemon:\n31\t    def __init__(self, store: Optional[SpineStore] = None, *, trusted_pubkey: Optional[str] = None):\n32\t        from ..governor.identity import owner_pubkey\n33\t        self.store = store or SpineStore()\n34\t        # tts=a.tts, tts_voice=a.tts_voice)\n243\t    print(f\"  transcript: {p.transcript!r}\")\n244\t    print(f\"  response:   {p.response!r}\")\n245\t    print(f\"  spoke →     {a.out}\")\n246\t    print(f\"  events:     {p.events}\")\n247\t\n248\t\n249\tdef cmd_warden_anchor_set(a) -> None:\n250\t    \"\"\"Cross-anchor the WARDEN action-log head into the append-only spine (anti-rollback).\n251\t    AUTHENTICATED: the (count, head_hash, pubkey) tuple must carry a valid Ed25519 signature by\n252\t    the WARDEN key `pubkey`, so a rogue local caller cannot POISON the high-water (e.g. set a\n253\t    huge count to make every future verify fail). Only the KERNEL, which holds the WARDEN private\n254\t    key, can anchor.\"\"\"\n255\t    if not _verify_ed25519(_warden_anchor_msg(int(a.count), a.head_hash, a.pubkey), a.sig, a.pubkey):\n256\t        print(\"REJECTED: warden-anchor-set signature invalid (only the WARDEN key may anchor)\", file=sys.stderr)\n257\t        sys.exit(2)\n258\t    store = SpineStore()\n259\t    store.append(kind=\"warden_checkpoint\", source=\"warden\", actor=\"warden\",\n260\t                 payload={\"count\": int(a.count), \"head_hash\": a.head_hash, \"pubkey\": a.pubkey})\n261\t    checkpoint(store)  # re-sign the spine head so the anchor sits under the spine's signature (anti-truncation)\n262\t    print(f\"anchored WARDEN head into spine: count={a.count} head={a.head_hash[:16]}\")\n263\t\n264\t\n265\tdef cmd_warden_anchor_get(a) -> None:\n266\t    \"\"\"Print the highest WARDEN head ever anchored FOR THIS KEY, as JSON {count, head_hash}.\n267\t    FAILS CLOSED (exit 2) if the spine's own integrity does not hold — otherwise a surgical edit\n268\t    to a warden_checkpoint line, or a spine tail-truncation removing recent anchors, would silently\n269\t    lower the high-water and let a rolled-back WARDEN log pass verify. Scoped by pubkey so a key\n270\t    rotation starts a fresh lineage.\"\"\"\n271\t    import json as _json\n272\t    store = SpineStore()\n273\t    ok, msg = store.verify()                       # chain: catches a tampered/deleted anchor record\n274\t    if not ok:\n275\t        print(f\"REJECTED: spine integrity failed — {msg}\", file=sys.stderr)\n276\t        sys.exit(2)\n277\t    hok, hmsg = verify_checkpoint(store)           # signed head: catches spine tail-truncation\n278\t    if not hok and \"TAMPER\" in hmsg.upper():\n279\t        print(f\"REJECTED: spine head tampered — {hmsg}\", file=sys.stderr)\n280\t        sys.exit(2)\n281\t    best_count, best_hash = 0, \"\"\n282\t    for r in store.iter_records():\n283\t        if r.kind == \"warden_checkpoint\" and r.payload.get(\"pubkey\") == a.pubkey:\n284\t            c = int(r.payload.get(\"count\", 0))\n285\t            if c >= best_count:\n286\t                best_count, best_hash = c, r.payload.get(\"head_hash\", \"\")\n287\t    print(_json.dumps({\"count\": best_count, \"head_hash\": best_hash}))\n288\t\n289\t\n290\tdef cmd_warden(a) -> None:\n291\t    \"\"\"Phase 6 governor controls (SIGIL §5): kill switch + per-kind promotion policy. Governance\n292\t    mutations are signed by the persisted OWNER key (auto-created once if absent).\"\"\"\n293\t    from .governor import KillSwitch, PromotionPolicy\n294\t    from .governor.identity import ensure_owner_keypair, owner_pubkey\n295\t    store = SpineStore()\n296\t    if a.action == \"status\":\n297\t        print(f\"  kill switch: {'ENGAGED (mesh halted)' if KillSwitch(store).is_engaged() else 'released (mesh live)'}\")\n298\t        return\n299\t    ok = ensure_owner_keypair()   # owner signing key (the trust anchor)\n300\t    if a.action == \"kill\":\n301\t        seq = KillSwitch(store, owner_key=ok).engage(reason=a.reason or \"\")\n302\t        print(f\"  KILL SWITCH ENGAGED (seq {seq}) — agent mesh halted; perception + memory read stay alive\")\n303\t    elif a.action == \"release\":\n304\t        seq = KillSwitch(store, owner_key=ok).release(reason=a.reason or \"\")\n305\t        print(f\"  kill switch released (seq {seq}, owner-signed) — agent mesh live again\")\n306\t    elif a.action == \"promote\":\n307\t        seq = PromotionPolicy(store, owner_key=ok).grant(a.agent, a.scope or \"*\")\n308\t        print(f\"  refused: {a.agent} has no promotion path (SIGIL §4.6)\" if seq is None\n309\t              else f\"  promoted {a.agent}/{a.scope or '*'} → A2 auto-approve, owner-signed (seq {seq})\")\n310\t    elif a.action == \"revoke\":\n311\t        seq = PromotionPolicy(store, owner_key=ok).revoke(a.agent, a.scope or \"*\")\n312\t        print(f\"  revoked promotion for {a.agent}/{a.scope or '*'} (seq {seq})\")\n313\t\n314\t\n315\tdef cmd_audit(a) -> None:\n316\t    from .audit import render_audit, self_audit\n317\t    store = SpineStore()\n318\t    rows = self_audit(store, agent=a.agent)\n319\t    print(render_audit(rows, agent=a.agent))\n320\t\n321\t\n322\tdef cmd_approve(a) -> None:\n323\t    from .agents.approvals import ApprovalQueue\n324\t    from .governor.identity import ensure_owner_keypair\n325\t    owner_key = ensure_owner_keypair()   # noqa: BLE001\n332\t        print(f\"  cannot {a.decision} seq {a.seq}: {e}\")\n333\t\n334\t\n335\tdef cmd_dashboard(a) -> None:\n336\t    from .dashboard import render_dashboard, snapshot\n337\t    print(render_dashboard(snapshot(SpineStore())))\n338\t\n339\t\n340\tdef cmd_scrape(a) -> None:\n341\t    \"\"\"SCRIBE grounded web research — crawl PUBLIC, scope-gated, robots-respecting, serve-the-quote.\"\"\"\n342\t    from .scrape import ScrapeScope\n343\t    from .scrape.researcher import WebResearcher\n344\t    from .spine.store import SpineStore\n345\t    if not a.scope_domain:\n346\t        print(\"  --scope-domain is required (deny-all by default): e.g. --scope-domain example.com\")\n347\t        return\n348\t    scope = ScrapeScope(a.scope_domain, include_subdomains=a.subdomains)\n349\t    store = SpineStore()\n350\t    res = WebResearcher(store).research_web(a.question or \"\", a.seed or [], scope)\n351\t    print(f\"  {'; '.join(res.notes)}\")\n352\t    for seq in res.applied:\n353\t        rec = store.get(seq)\n354\t        if rec and rec.payload.get(\"signal\") == \"web.research\":\n355\t            print(\"\\n\" + rec.payload.get(\"text\", \"\"))\n356\t\n357\t\n358\tdef cmd_host(a) -> None:\n359\t    \"\"\"Show this host's capability descriptor (WS-D) — what the mesh routes on.\"\"\"\n360\t    from .platform import host\n361\t    d = host().capabilities()\n362\t    print(f\"  host {d.host_id} · {d.os}\")\n363\t    print(f\"    screen={d.has_screen} camera={d.has_camera} gpu_vlm={d.has_gpu_vlm} always_on={d.always_on}\")\n364\t\n365\t\n366\tdef _device_fingerprint(pubkey: str) -> str:\n367\t    \"\"\"A short, human-verifiable fingerprint of a device pubkey — first 8 bytes of its SHA-256 as\n368\t    `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`. The PC and the future phone client MUST compute this identically so the\n369\t    operator can eyeball-match the code the phone shows before authorizing (defeats a key swap).\"\"\"\n370\t    short = sha256_hex(pubkey.encode())[:16]\n371\t    return \"-\".join(short[i:i + 4] for i in range(0, 16, 4))\n372\t\n373\t\n374\tdef _mesh_authorize(store, device_id, pubkey, owner_key, *, assume_yes=False, confirm=input):\n375\t    \"\"\"Authorize a phone device key (owner-signed). Prints the fingerprint and, unless `assume_yes`,\n376\t    makes the operator confirm it matches what the phone displays before writing the ledger record.\n377\t    Returns the record seq, or None if the operator did not confirm.\"\"\"\n378\t    fp = _device_fingerprint(pubkey)\n379\t    print(f\"  device {device_id!r} fingerprint: {fp}\")\n380\t    if not assume_yes:\n381\t        ans = confirm(f\"  confirm this fingerprint matches what phone {device_id!r} shows? [yes/no] \")\n382\t        if (ans or \"\").strip().lower() != \"yes\":\n383\t            print(\"  aborted — fingerprint not confirmed; device NOT authorized\")\n384\t            return None\n385\t    seq = authorize_device(store, device_id, pubkey, owner_key)\n386\t    print(f\"  authorized device {device_id!r} (owner-signed, seq {seq}); fingerprint {fp}\")\n387\t    return seq\n388\t\n389\t\n390\tdef _mesh_revoke(store, device_id, pubkey, owner_key):\n391\t    \"\"\"Revoke a phone device key (owner-signed). Returns the record seq.\"\"\"\n392\t    seq = revoke_device(store, device_id, pubkey, owner_key)\n393\t    print(f\"  revoked device {device_id!r} (owner-signed, seq {seq}); fingerprint {_device_fingerprint(pubkey)}\")\n394\t    return seq\n395\t\n396\t\n397\tdef _mesh_list(store, owner_pubkey):\n398\t    \"\"\"Print the currently-authorized device keys (owner-signed authorize minus later revoke).\n399\t    Returns the set for callers/tests.\"\"\"\n400\t    devices = authorized_devices(store, owner_pubkey)\n401\t    if not devices:\n402\t        print(\"  no authorized devices\")\n403\t    else:\n404\t        print(f\"  {len(devices)} authorized device key(s):\")\n405\t        for pub in sorted(devices):\n406\t            print(f\"    {pub}  [{_device_fingerprint(pub)}]\")\n407\t    return devices\n408\t\n409\t\n410\tdef cmd_mesh(a) -> None:\n411\t    \"\"\"Phase 9 W1-E — the PC-side mesh pairing back-end: authorize / revoke / list phone device keys.\n412\t    Authorizations are owner-signed via the PERSISTED owner identity (never a supplied key); a thin\n413\t    wrapper over the tested mesh ledger. `list-devices` needs no signing (a fail-closed read).\"\"\"\n414\t    from .governor.identity import ensure_owner_keypair, owner_pubkey\n415\t    store = SpineStore()\n416\t    if a.action == \"list-devices\":\n417\t        _mesh_list(store, owner_pubkey())\n418\t        return\n419\t    if not a.device_id or not a.pubkey:\n420\t        print(f\"  usage: sigil mesh {a.action} <device-id> <pubkey>\", file=sys.stderr)\n421\t        sys.exit(2)\n422\t    owner = ensure_owner_keypair()   # the persisted owner key IS the trusted signer (doctrine)\n423\t    if a.action == \"authorize\":\n424\t        _mesh_authorize(store, a.device_id, a.pubkey, owner, assume_yes=a.yes)\n425\t    elif a.action == \"revoke\":\n426\t        _mesh_revoke(store, a.device_id, a.pubkey, owner)\n427\t\n428\t\n429\tdef cmd_serve(a) -> None:\n430\t    \"\"\"Start the loopback glass-cockpit UI. loopback/private only — NO wire secret)\")\n    print(\"  pair a phone (owner, at the desktop):  sigil mesh authorize <device-id> <device-pubkey>\")\n    print(\"  every request must carry an authorized-device signature (X-SIGIL-Envelope) — there is no token\")\n    try:\n        srv.serve_forever()\n    except KeyboardInterrupt:\n        srv.shutdown()","new_string":"def _write_secure(path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write `data` to `path` created 0600 up-front (no world-readable window) — the vault/secrets\n    secure-file idiom (`os.open(..., 0o600)`).\"\"\"\n    fd = os.open(str(path), os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)\n    with os.fdopen(fd, \"wb\") as fh:\n        fh.write(data)\n\n\ndef _fingerprint(cert) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The pinned identity: sha256 of the DER cert, hex, colon-grouped byte pairs (openssl-style,\n    upper-case) — what the owner eyeball-matches on the phone once.\"\"\"\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes\n    h = cert.fingerprint(hashes.SHA256()).hex().upper()      # fingerprint() == sha256 of the DER encoding\n    return \":\".join(h[i:i + 2] for i in range(0, len(h), 2))\n\n\ndef ensure_bridge_cert(addr: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Mint (or REUSE) a minimal owner-pinned self-signed TLS cert for the bridge bound to `addr`,\n    returning `(certfile, keyfile, sha256_fingerprint)`.\n\n    The cert carries `addr` as its CN and (when `addr` is an IP — always true for a `bind_ok` bridge)\n    as an `x509.IPAddress` SubjectAlternativeName, so an IP-literal TLS connection matches. Cert+key\n    live under `SIGIL_HOME/bridge/` (dir 0700, files 0600). If a cert already exists FOR THIS ADDR it\n    is REUSED — the fingerprint is therefore STABLE across restarts, so the owner pins it exactly once\n    (a changed fingerprint later means a MITM / a wiped key, not a benign restart). An EC P-256 key is\n    used (easy for `cryptography`, accepted by `ssl`). Validity ~2 years; a real wallclock is fine here\n    (this is TLS notBefore/notAfter, not spine or learning math).\"\"\"\n    import datetime\n    import ipaddress as _ip\n\n    from cryptography import x509\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes, serialization\n    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import ec\n    from cryptography.x509.oid import NameOID\n\n    from ..config import SIGIL_HOME                          # read at call-time (patchable in tests)\n\n    bridge_dir = Path(SIGIL_HOME) / \"bridge\"\n    bridge_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    try:\n        os.chmod(bridge_dir, 0o700)                          # owner-only, like the spine/keys dirs\n    except OSError:\n        pass\n    tag = addr.replace(\":\", \"_\").replace(\"/\", \"_\").replace(\"%\", \"_\")   # one stable cert per bind addr\n    certfile = bridge_dir / f\"cert-{tag}.pem\"\n    keyfile = bridge_dir / f\"key-{tag}.pem\"\n\n    if certfile.is_file() and keyfile.is_file():             # REUSE → stable fingerprint (pin once)\n        cert = x509.load_pem_x509_certificate(certfile.read_bytes())\n        return str(certfile), str(keyfile), _fingerprint(cert)\n\n    key = ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())\n    name = x509.Name([x509.NameAttribute(NameOID.COMMON_NAME, addr)])\n    try:                                                     # bind addr is an IP by construction (bind_ok)\n        san = x509.SubjectAlternativeName([x509.IPAddress(_ip.ip_address(addr))])\n    except ValueError:                                       # defensive: a hostname would use a DNS SAN\n        san = x509.SubjectAlternativeName([x509.DNSName(addr)])\n    now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)       # real wallclock (tz-aware; TLS validity, not spine math)\n    cert = (\n        x509.CertificateBuilder()\n        .subject_name(name)\n        .issuer_name(name)                                   # self-signed: issuer == subject\n        .public_key(key.public_key())\n        .serial_number(x509.random_serial_number())\n        .not_valid_before(now - datetime.timedelta(minutes=5))   # small skew tolerance\n        .not_valid_after(now + datetime.timedelta(days=730))     # ~2 years\n        .add_extension(san, critical=False)\n        .add_extension(x509.BasicConstraints(ca=False, path_length=None), critical=True)\n        .sign(key, hashes.SHA256())\n    )\n    _write_secure(certfile, cert.public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM))\n    _write_secure(keyfile, key.private_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM,\n                                             serialization.PrivateFormat.PKCS8,\n                                             serialization.NoEncryption()))\n    return str(certfile), str(keyfile), _fingerprint(cert)\n\n\ndef serve(*, addr: str, port: int = _DEFAULT_PORT, spine_path=None, tls: bool = True) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run the WireGuard-bound bridge transport. Use TLS unless you terminate it upstream in the tunnel.\")\n    print(\"  pair a phone (owner, at the desktop):  sigil mesh authorize <device-id> <device-pubkey>\")\n    print(\"  every request must carry an authorized-device signature (X-SIGIL-Envelope) — there is no token\")\n    try:\n        srv.serve_forever()\n    except KeyboardInterrupt:\n        srv.shutdown()"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":767,"cache_read_input_tokens":83509,"output_tokens":2975,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":767},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2975,"cache_read_input_tokens":83509,"cache_creation_input_tokens":767,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":767,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CdAS6Up69TzApCTozHDH8","attributionAgent":"general-purpose","type":"assistant","uuid":"9995f5a1-8a08-4a8a-8b45-90a2a5171a80","timestamp":"2026-07-19T00:01:28.785Z","effort":"xhigh","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"7591b3f0-63ce-427e-a006-3ee98f33dda1","isSidechain":true,"agentId":"a4cc60b3258bed6fb","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdASBYitAxQedTV56ngKo","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Xo96kQR6g8vFXwPziLmRLy","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/kali/sigil/tests/test_bridge_tls.py","content":"\"\"\"SIGIL Phase 9 W1-D — the bridge's owner-pinned self-signed TLS slice: the cert helper\n(`ensure_bridge_cert`) that mints a minimal self-signed cert with the WG IP as a SubjectAlternativeName,\nstores cert+key owner-only (dir 0700 / files 0600) under `SIGIL_HOME/bridge/`, and REUSES it so the\nsha256 fingerprint is STABLE across restarts (the owner pins it once). Also asserts the bind guard\nstill refuses a public address for `bridge serve` (fail-closed, minting no cert), plus a loopback TLS\nhandshake smoke test proving the wrapped socket serves a real HTTPS envelope.\n\nDeterministic by construction: `SIGIL_HOME` is redirected to a fresh temp dir per test and removed\nafter. No real owner identity, no network beyond loopback:0.\nRun: ~/.sigil/venv/bin/python tests/test_bridge_tls.py\"\"\"\nimport contextlib\nimport hashlib\nimport os\nimport shutil\nimport stat\nimport tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport sigil.config as sconfig\nfrom cryptography import x509\nfrom cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization\nfrom cryptography.x509.oid import NameOID\n\nfrom sigil.bridge.daemon import bind_ok\nfrom sigil.bridge.server import ensure_bridge_cert\n\n\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef temp_home():\n    \"\"\"Redirect SIGIL_HOME to a throwaway dir so `ensure_bridge_cert` (which reads\n    `sigil.config.SIGIL_HOME` at call-time) writes into it, and restore + clean up after.\"\"\"\n    orig = sconfig.SIGIL_HOME\n    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=\"sigil-tls-\")\n    sconfig.SIGIL_HOME = Path(d)\n    try:\n        yield Path(d)\n    finally:\n        sconfig.SIGIL_HOME = orig\n        shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)\n\n\n# ---- the cert helper mints a usable cert+key under SIGIL_HOME/bridge/ -----------------------------\ndef test_ensure_bridge_cert_creates_cert_and_key():\n    with temp_home() as home:\n        certfile, keyfile, fp = ensure_bridge_cert(\"127.0.0.1\")\n        assert Path(certfile).is_file(), \"a cert file is produced\"\n        assert Path(keyfile).is_file(), \"a key file is produced\"\n        assert Path(certfile).parent == home / \"bridge\", \"cert lives under SIGIL_HOME/bridge/\"\n        # fingerprint = 32 colon-grouped hex byte pairs of a sha256\n        pairs = fp.split(\":\")\n        assert len(pairs) == 32 and all(len(p) == 2 for p in pairs), \\\n            \"fingerprint is sha256 (32 bytes) as colon-grouped hex pairs\"\n        assert fp == fp.upper(), \"fingerprint hex is upper-case (openssl-style)\"\n\n\n# ---- the cert + key are owner-only (secure-file idiom) --------------------------------------------\ndef test_cert_files_are_owner_only():\n    with temp_home():\n        certfile, keyfile, _ = ensure_bridge_cert(\"127.0.0.1\")\n        assert stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(keyfile).st_mode) == 0o600, \"the private key is 0600\"\n        assert stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(certfile).st_mode) == 0o600, \"the cert is 0600\"\n        assert stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(Path(certfile).parent).st_mode) == 0o700, \"the bridge dir is 0700\"\n\n\n# ---- REUSE: the fingerprint is stable across restarts (pin once) ----------------------------------\ndef test_fingerprint_stable_across_calls_reuse_not_regenerate():\n    with temp_home():\n        cf1, kf1, fp1 = ensure_bridge_cert(\"127.0.0.1\")\n        key1 = Path(kf1).read_bytes()                        # capture the FIRST key material\n        cf2, kf2, fp2 = ensure_bridge_cert(\"127.0.0.1\")      # second call must REUSE, not regenerate\n        assert (cf1, kf1) == (cf2, kf2), \"the same cert/key paths are used for the same addr\"\n        assert fp1 == fp2, \"the fingerprint is STABLE across calls (the owner pins it exactly once)\"\n        assert Path(kf2).read_bytes() == key1, \"the key file was NOT regenerated (byte-identical)\"\n\n\n# ---- a fresh addr gets its OWN stable cert (not a shared one) -------------------------------------\ndef test_distinct_addr_gets_distinct_cert():\n    with temp_home():\n        _, _, fp_lo = ensure_bridge_cert(\"127.0.0.1\")\n        _, kf_wg, fp_wg = ensure_bridge_cert(\"10.7.0.2\")     # a WireGuard-style private addr\n        assert Path(kf_wg).is_file(), \"a distinct addr mints its own cert\"\n        assert fp_lo != fp_wg, \"different bind addresses get independent (distinct) certs\"\n\n\n# ---- the cert parses and carries the WG IP as a SubjectAlternativeName ----------------------------\ndef test_cert_parses_and_has_ip_san_and_matching_fingerprint():\n    with temp_home():\n        certfile, _, fp = ensure_bridge_cert(\"10.7.0.2\")\n        cert = x509.load_pem_x509_certificate(Path(certfile).read_bytes())\n        san = cert.extensions.get_extension_for_class(x509.SubjectAlternativeName)\n        ips = [str(ip) for ip in san.value.get_values_for_type(x509.IPAddress)]\n        assert \"10.7.0.2\" in ips, \"the WG IP is a SubjectAlternativeName (x509.IPAddress)\"\n        cn = cert.subject.get_attributes_for_oid(NameOID.COMMON_NAME)[0].value\n        assert cn == \"10.7.0.2\", \"the CN is the bind addr\"\n        # independently recompute the fingerprint: sha256 of the DER cert, colon-grouped upper hex\n        der = cert.public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.DER)\n        h = hashlib.sha256(der).hexdigest().upper()\n        expect = \":\".join(h[i:i + 2] for i in range(0, len(h), 2))\n        assert fp == expect, \"the returned fingerprint == sha256(DER cert)\"\n\n\n# ---- the bind guard still refuses a public addr for `bridge serve` (fail-closed, no cert) ---------\ndef test_bridge_serve_refuses_public_addr_and_mints_no_cert():\n    assert bind_ok(\"127.0.0.1\") is True, \"loopback binds\"\n    assert bind_ok(\"10.7.0.2\") is True, \"a private WireGuard addr binds\"\n    for bad in (\"0.0.0.0\", \"::\", \"8.8.8.8\", \"1.2.3.4\"):\n        assert bind_ok(bad) is False, f\"a public/unspecified addr ({bad}) is refused\"\n    # the CLI handler fails closed on a public addr, BEFORE ensure_bridge_cert → no cert dir created\n    from sigil.cli import cmd_bridge_serve\n\n    class _Args:\n        addr, port, no_tls = \"8.8.8.8\", 8734, False\n\n    with temp_home() as home:\n        try:\n            cmd_bridge_serve(_Args())\n            assert False, \"cmd_bridge_serve must refuse a public bind address\"\n        except SystemExit as e:\n            assert e.code == 2, \"a refused public bind exits 2 (fail-closed)\"\n        assert not (home / \"bridge\").exists(), \"no cert was minted for a refused public bind\"\n\n\n# ---- loopback TLS smoke: the wrapped listener serves a real HTTPS envelope ------------------------\ndef test_loopback_tls_handshake_serves_a_real_https_envelope():\n    import json\n    import ssl\n    import threading\n    import time\n    import urllib.error\n    import urllib.request\n\n    from sigil.bridge.server import build_server\n    from sigil.reuse import generate_keypair\n\n    with temp_home():\n        owner = generate_keypair()                           # inject a pubkey → never touches real owner identity\n        spine = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".jsonl\")\n        srv = build_server(addr=\"127.0.0.1\", port=0, spine_path=spine,\n                           trusted_pubkey=owner.public_key_b64)\n        certfile, keyfile, _ = ensure_bridge_cert(\"127.0.0.1\")\n        ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)\n        ctx.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile)\n        srv.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(srv.socket, server_side=True)   # exactly what serve() does\n        port = srv.server_address[1]\n        threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()\n        time.sleep(0.05)\n        try:\n            # a client that TRUSTS the pinned self-signed cert (CERT_REQUIRED against our cafile);\n            # skip hostname matching for a robust IP-literal handshake across ssl versions.\n            cctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certfile)\n            cctx.check_hostname = False\n            req = urllib.request.Request(f\"https://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/pending\")\n            try:\n                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=5, context=cctx) as r:\n                    code, body = r.status, r.read().decode()\n            except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:              # 401 (no envelope) is still an HTTPS response\n                code, body = e.code, e.read().decode()\n            assert code == 401, \"the TLS handshake completed and the server answered over HTTPS\"\n            assert json.loads(body).get(\"error\"), \"a valid JSON envelope was served over the pinned TLS socket\"\n        finally:\n            srv.shutdown()\n            srv.server_close()\n            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):\n                os.unlink(spine)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    fns = [v for k, v in sorted(globals().items()) if k.startswith(\"test_\")]\n    passed = 0\n    for fn in fns:\n        try:\n            fn(); print(f\"  PASS  {fn.__name__}\"); passed += 1\n        except AssertionError as e:\n            print(f\"  FAIL  {fn.__name__}: {e}\")\n        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n            import traceback\n            print(f\"  ERROR {fn.__name__}: {e}\")\n            traceback.print_exc()\n    print(f\"{passed}/{len(fns)} Phase-9 W1-D (owner-pinned self-signed bridge TLS) guarantees hold\")\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":588,"cache_read_input_tokens":88113,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":588,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CdASBWgbddNrQn3k3x98g","attributionAgent":"general-purpose","type":"assistant","uuid":"916f3c21-6db6-4931-9f98-a032618f910a","timestamp":"2026-07-19T00:02:45.469Z","effort":"xhigh","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}
